description: Frozen database baseline. Every value here is a claim the migration-replay job re-proves from an empty PostgreSQL 17 on every run. A value that changes legitimately must be raised in the SAME commit that changes the schema, so the diff shows both.
establishedBy: P1-21 Inventory Backend, hosted clean room at 96c93cadcba573e34f97f8f6ea7814c2f707abeb
structuralTotalsEstablishedBy: PR CI run 19 (run id 30431556718), job `database-migration-replay / migration-replay`, artifact `evidence-migration-replay`, file `migration-replay.json`, at feature head 8d7bfff09cf914e00ff5ff4587341ece261185c3, started 2026-07-29T07:24:48Z, GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest, PostgreSQL 17 service container replayed from empty.
migrationCountNote: 119 through DBCR-P1-16-001. Raised to 120 by DBCR-P1-18-001 (20260731090000_rec_custody_release_visit_marker.sql), which closes P1-27-INT-013 — a Vehicle could be received exactly once, ever, because the terminal status `converted` sat inside the predicate of uq_reception_visits_open_vehicle. NOT raised to 121 by P1-OD-025, which adds 20260815090000_shared_reception_evidence_foundation.sql and therefore makes the tree hold 121. The reason is in pendingMeasurementNote: this figure is double-bound, and raising it alone breaks a gate.
forbiddenMigrationPrefixNote: This reserves a FILENAME series, not an ordinal. It forbids files literally beginning `120` — the `120_`/`120…_` shape a future phase would mint — and it is unrelated to a migration merely being the 120th in the tree. DBCR-P1-18-001 is the 120th migration and is named `20260731090000_…`, so it does not match and this pin stays exactly as it was. Do not 'reconcile' the two numbers: they measure different things, and weakening this to accommodate an ordinal would retire a real guard.
schemaHashNote: Produced by `npm run validate:schema-inventory -- --hash-only`, over the 17 RootLco business schemas only — which is why it reproduces on a developer's Supabase stack even though the structural totals below do not. Was a677eb05… from P1-18 through DBCR-P1-16-001. Raised here by DBCR-P1-18-001, which adds rec.reception_visits.custody_released_at, two rec functions and two triggers, and replaces uq_reception_visits_open_vehicle. The new value was measured locally BEFORE being copied from CI, and the two agreed digit for digit; a baseline raised from a CI log alone would only be recording that the log said something.
permissionCountNote: 100 through P1-21 and unchanged by P1-22, which declared only codes P1-11 had already seeded. P1-23 raised it to 104 by adding the four READ codes its operations declare: shared.notification.read, shared.notification.delivery.read, shared.document.archive and rpt.report.read. The P1-27 read-surface remediation (executed by P1-18) raised it to 107 with apt.appointment.read, rec.reception.read and rec.reception.close: P1-18 had seeded no read code because it exposed no read operation, and no closure code because closed_without_work/refused were unreachable — both facts that remediation ended (P1-27-INT-010..021, -014, -018, -019). The intake-catalogue MANAGEMENT remediation raises it to 109 with apt.catalogue.manage and rec.catalogue.manage: the seven configuration catalogues ship zero rows by the no-fake-data policy and no operation could add one, so a required appointmentTypeId could never be satisfied — the reads alone did not make the screens usable (P1-27-INT-018). Both are new codes rather than a reuse of apt.appointment.manage / rec.reception.manage, because booking an appointment and defining what the types ARE are different authorities. Added to supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql, which is idempotent and additive — NOT a migration, so migrationCount stays 120 and schemaHash is unchanged. This pin did its job once already: four P1-23 codes were declared by routes and missing from the catalog, and every denial-based authorization test still passed, because a permission that does not exist cannot be held by anybody. P1-OD-025 raises it to 110 with shared.document.read, so reading evidence no longer requires shared.document.manage, the authority that CREATES it. The code is both seeded (04_iam_permission_catalog.sql) and inserted by the migration with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so an environment that migrated without re-seeding still resolves it; both paths are idempotent and the count is one either way.
structuralTotalsDeltaNote: DBCR-P1-18-001 raised `functions` 514 -> 516 and `triggers` 541 -> 543; `tables`, `policies` and `security_definer` are untouched. The delta is +2 functions (rec.guard_custody_release_marker, rec.apply_custody_release) and +2 triggers (tg_reception_visits_custody_release_marker, tg_custody_history_apply_release), read off the migration rather than measured, BECAUSE these totals cannot be reproduced locally: they count every non-system schema, and a developer's Supabase stack carries auth/storage/realtime objects the CI plain-postgres container does not. Measured on the local stack the same queries return tables 292, functions 591, triggers 548 and security_definer 6 — none of which is comparable with the figures above. The schemaHash IS reproducible locally and was reproduced; these four are the ones CI alone can settle.
structuralTotalsNote: Recorded from the first GitHub-hosted run, using migration-replay-checks.mjs's OWN catalog queries. The earlier note warned that copying earlier phase-gate numbers across would compare two things that were never the same measurement, and run 19 proved that warning exact: `functions` here is 514, while scripts/db/schema-inventory.mjs reported 212 for the same database in the same run.
functionCountDiscrepancyNote: 518 and 216 are both correct; they count different populations, and the difference is entirely in the WHERE clause. migration-replay-checks.mjs counts `pg_proc` filtered only by `n.nspname NOT IN ('pg_catalog','information_schema')`, so it includes extension and public-namespace functions. schema-inventory.mjs counts `WHERE n.nspname = ANY($1)`, restricted to the 17 RootLco business schemas — and the per-schema breakdown in that same artifact sums to exactly 216 (org, iam, shared, crm, veh, apt, rec, wo, tech, dia, qms, svc, quo, inv, sal, wty, rpt). The 302-function difference is therefore extension-owned code, not RootLco code, and it is constant: the pair moved 514/212 -> 516/214 together when DBCR-P1-18-001 added two rec functions, and 516/214 -> 518/216 together when the P1-OD-025 evidence foundation added shared.begin_document_scan and shared.complete_document_scan — which is what lets each step be derived rather than guessed. Neither figure was chosen for convenience: 518 belongs HERE because this file is enforced by the script that produces 518, and 216 remains the number to quote for RootLco's own schema and the one comparable with every prior phase gate. Do not 'reconcile' them by editing either.
structuralTotalsCrossChecks: tables 242, triggers 541 and policies 631 are identical under both scripts, and the hosted clean room independently reported 242 live tables, 999 indexes and 537 foreign keys. Only `functions` diverges.
seededStructuralTablesNote: Enumerated from an empty PostgreSQL 17 in run 19 after migrations and seeding, when iam.permissions held 100 rows (104 since P1-23; the row counts below are that run's record, not a pin): iam.permissions (100 rows), inv.units_of_measure (12), sal.payment_methods (3), wo.job_states (6), wo.job_transitions (10), wo.work_order_states (9), wo.work_order_transitions (15). Every one is a structural catalog — permissions, units, payment methods and the work-order state machine — and none is business data, so the no-fake-data policy holds: a freshly provisioned database still starts with no customers, vehicles, orders or invoices. Now that the list is recorded, migration-replay-checks.mjs FAILS on any populated business table outside it, which is the point of recording it. Row counts are deliberately not pinned; the check matches table names only, so seeding one more permission is not a build break.
seededStructuralTablesAsymmetryNote: The check flags UNEXPECTED populated tables, not missing ones. A seed that silently stops running therefore still passes this particular gate — it is caught elsewhere, by the smoke reads and by permissionCount (100 when this note was written, 104 since P1-23 — see permissionCountNote).
pendingMeasurementNote: UNMEASURED AND DELIBERATELY UNRAISED AT THIS COMMIT: migrationCount, schemaHash and structuralTotals. The P1-OD-025 branch adds migration 20260815090000_shared_reception_evidence_foundation.sql, so the tree holds 121 .sql files and migration-replay-checks.mjs will report "migration count is 121, the recorded baseline is 120" the next time it runs. All three must move together, in one commit, taken from one database run. WHY NOT JUST RAISE migrationCount: the "Migrations applied" row on docs/phase-1/phase-1-27/clean-room-evidence.md is bound by TWO tests in tests/ci/p1-27-doc-counts.test.ts that disagree the moment this baseline moves past the superseded head. "states the migration count the superseded head really held" (:603) requires the row to equal the count at 356f1a1e, which is 120 forever, because a historical measurement does not change. "quotes the schema hash and migration count the committed baseline carries" (:724) requires the same row to equal this baseline. One row, one historical reference point and one current one. Raising this figure alone therefore turns one red gate into a different red gate, and edits a superseded phase record in the process. WHAT TO DO: in the same commit, run a database, re-measure schemaHash with "npm run validate:schema-inventory -- --hash-only" and structuralTotals from migration-replay-checks.mjs own catalog queries, raise all three, and separate the two bindings on that clean-room row so a historical figure stops being compared to a current baseline. The migration adds two columns and a CHECK on shared.document_categories, two columns, a replaced CHECK and a new CHECK on shared.document_versions, and two functions in the shared schema, so none of the three is unchanged. permissionCount IS raised here (109 to 110) because it is bound in exactly one place besides this file, tests/db/p1-15-shared-services-runtime-capabilities.test.ts, which moved with it, and it is derivable from supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql without a database.
securityDefinerPolicyNote: OPEN DECISION, deliberately not resolved on the branch that raised it. scripts/ci/migration-replay-checks.mjs hard-codes security_definer !== 0 as a failure ("the approved count is 0"). That is a rule inside the script, not a value in this file, so it cannot be raised by editing the baseline. Migration 20260815090000 adds TWO: shared.begin_document_scan and shared.complete_document_scan. Both pin an empty search_path, both are REVOKEd from PUBLIC and GRANTed only to app_runtime, and both re-check tenant, actor, permission and source state on every call. They exist because the alternative is worse: granting app_runtime INSERT on shared.file_scan_results would let request code write its own clean verdict, which is exactly the withholding that keeps accepted out of reach of request code and which three existing suites assert. Somebody must choose between raising the approved count to 2 with this justification recorded, moving the scan to the app_worker role, or accepting the weaker grant. Nothing was weakened unilaterally.
